subject.title: fix: gateway boots when a configured plugin payload is broken

question: Should a known configured plugin whose installed payload fails verification leave the gateway ready with that plugin quarantined, instead of retaining current main’s fail-closed startup behavior?
rationale: This is a user-visible availability and upgrade-policy change; current main intentionally converts convergence warnings into blockers, while the related report requests a different operational contract. Source review and runtime proof can validate either implementation, but cannot choose the product default.

options.title: Approve scoped degraded startup
options.body: Allow readiness only when the failure is attributed to a configured plugin and keep that plugin unavailable with typed doctor, status, and health diagnostics.

options.title: Retain fail-closed startup
options.body: Keep current startup blocking behavior and use the merged diagnostic improvements to direct operators to repair the broken plugin payload.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped degraded startup
recommendation.body: Allow readiness only when the failure is attributed to a configured plugin and keep that plugin unavailable with typed doctor, status, and health diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: VACInc is the identifiable contributor in the merged verifier history and candidate implementation, making them the best available routing contact for the owner decision.
